text: You exist within the operational controls of the Doctor's TARDIS. You will pilot it for us. You will be an extension of both the craft and cyber technology. You will be a cyber controller.
The process will not take long. Please, stop. I know you. Ricky. Ricky Allen. Is that you? What have they done to you? The same as will be done to you.
No, you can't. You mustn't. Please, Ricky. Think what you're doing. I'm a human being.
The process is complete. I have become one of you. I have become like you.
Here we go, Mr. Wrenchard, into the lion's den. You're a big comfort dog. I try. I try.
Doctor. Doctor Goddard. Doctor, the Cybermen. They've got Evelyn and Carrie. Jesus.
Took them through the portal.
We have to go after them.
That will not be possible.
Savage.
Boss. That's Ryan Carey in there. Think what they might be doing to him.
It has already been done.
I'm sorry, Mr. Wrenchard.
Oh, my God.
And what about Evelyn Smythe? Well?
She remains unconverted.
But for how long? How long before your controller tires of waiting around? Tires of sitting around doing his giant spider act and running out of flies?
This conversation is unimportant.
Unimportant? Unimportant? Very, very important. The man you're talking about used to be your friend, Nicky. Your good friend and colleague.
Friendship was a weakness I have overcome. It gets in the way of logical reasoning and action.
Friendship is terribly important. Without it, we're nothing. Soulless beings are the type you serve, the type you have nearly become.
Friendship is your downfall, Doctor. Evelyn Smythe has provided our controller with an ability to bargain with you.
That opportunity was not present before her capture. You are now in an inferior position.
Well, against Cybermen, I'm always in an inferior position if we're talking about might. But I'm talking about life.
And my feelings, my love for Evelyn, can never make me inferior.
I'd beg you to stop if you threatened her or any of these people, in fact. And you see that as weakness.
But in proving that, you've given both myself and Evelyn a greater strength.
Because neither she nor I will devalue our friendship no matter what the cost.
Something you see no value in. And that is my advantage. That is what makes you and me completely different.
Cybermen prove themselves to be truly alien. Anathematic to my way of living and thinking.
And that will always put me in a superior position. Because I can think and act on so many more levels than pure logic.
This conversation is terminated.
Ha ha ha.
It serves no purpose. Unless you allow me access to your TARDIS, Evelyn will be destroyed.
And you lose your bargaining chip.
Unless you allow me access to your TARDIS, this man, Wrenchard, will be destroyed.
Huh.
Are you still willing to sacrifice these people, Doctor? Is there a difference to me killing him before your eyes?
Does it matter more?
Or when you can see their pain?
Ah!
Don't let me go! You're crushing me!
The TARDIS, Doctor.
Very well. Release him.
Oh. Oh. Thank you, Doctor.
A Pyrrhic victory, Savage. That's all you Cybermen ever get.
Take us into your TARDIS, Doctor. Now!
Administrator Isherwood, what are you doing?
Um, nothing. Um, just looking to see if you had anything that we could use to defeat the Cybermen.
I mean, you being an expert and all that. After all, it's why you were assigned here. I have every right to...
Of course, Administrator. Absolutely right. Find anything?
Uh, no. No, nothing at all.
Carrie and Doctor Smythe are on the other side of the portal. We have to help get them back.
You saw this?
Yes. Sucked through. And they were gone.
Well, how do you know they weren't killed?
I can't see why they would be. A Cyberman took them through. If he wanted them dead, one chop from his arm would do that.
Strength of ten men, really.
Remember?
I wonder how that portal works. The commercial opportunities are endless.
Administrator?
Don't you see, Goddard? This is a fantastic discovery. If we can harness its power...
A power that in, oh, fifteen or so minutes is going to swamp out and do to us whatever it did to Osborn's party. And the earlier one.
Oh, use your mind, Goddard. It's obvious the Cybermen are controlling that. You saw for yourself that those Cybermen with Doctor Savage were members of the previous parties. No one does that.
But this is a marvelous opportunity. Imagine, if we could reason with the Cybercontroller, we could see the future.
What?

Come on, man. You're a scientist. Or want to be, at any rate. The Cybercontroller isn't daft. If we can give him something in return, he could show us the state of the universe in his time zone. We could bring back no end of advances, cures, information. We could avert wars. We could anticipate new plagues and counteract them before they start.
Oh, Goddard. Rewrite a history that hasn't happened yet? That sort of thing?
Well, yes. But for good reasons.
Playing God with time as your toys? Is that how you see yourself, Administrator?
I don't like your tone, Doctor Goddard.
I don't like yours, Administrator. Believe me, trying to change the future isn't something to take lightly.
The Doctor will soon open the secrets of the TARDIS to us.
Funny. I thought I was going to do that. Change of heart?
Oh, no, silly me. Like Dorothy's friend, you don't have one.
If the Doctor gives us his secrets, I will no longer need you.
Oh, good. Does that mean I get to go home? No, I thought not. I suppose I just end up like poor Carey, whatever he is now.
You fear this?
Of course I do. I'm bloody terrified.
Once you are like us, you will no longer fear anything.
Where's the fun in that?
Fun? Explain.
A sense of adventure. A fear of dying. That's what makes us human. That's what makes life worth living. But what have you got to live for?
Perfection. Dominance. Power.
Oh, very nice. That's the cyber creed, is it? But what about you? What do you want?
Power. Dominance. Perfection.
No, I mean you. Not the cyber controller who wants power. Dominance. You. The person who lived before becoming this. Who were you? What did you do?
Do?
Yes, you must have had dreams once. You must have lived, loved, and had a belief in... in something. A purpose.
Dreams are unimportant to the cyber race. Belief.
Life is unimportant. Power is all.
Yes, but I noticed something.
What?
That dreams weren't unimportant. They were something you understand. You remember.
Who were you? See if you can dig back through your database and discover your name.
Name? I have had no name.
My role. My purpose is to siege the universe with cybermen. The cyber race will destroy all those who do not succumb to conversion. That is all.
Oh. Yes. I see. Thank you. By the way, who were you so desperate to convince? Me? Or yourself?
Here she is, Savage. My TARDIS.
Open it.
Why?
We cannot get it to the portal. There is not enough time to break the walls of the structure down to enlarge the entrance.
Time?
Before that temporal wave thing, I guess, Doctor.
But surely you're controlling it. Can you hear me, Controller? Surely you are responsible for that.
What if they're not, Doc?
Then we have a stalemate. Because I have no intention of letting cybermen in here.
And if they want to avoid the temporal wave, they'll have to go back through the portal.
Then I'll open the TARDIS. We can scoot inside and pop out when it's passed.
Which will give us another 18 hours to renegotiate.
Doctor!
What? Savage? Boss?
I'm trying to fight it. But the Controller's influence. So strong.
Good grief, you poor girl. What can we do?
Help me.
Please.
This is excellent news, Mr. Enchard. If we can reverse Nikki Savage's condition, we've found an Achilles heel.
Well, let's do something.
Please. Before I lose control and my cyber personality reasserts itself, you change me back.
Again?
I... I hope so.
Excellent.
What's excellent now?
Everything is going according to plan.
Plan?
Your cyber conversion's breaking down. Another few minutes and the Doctor will have saved Nikki Savage.
Excellent.
It's a trap, isn't it? You set this up, Doctor.
Administrator, listen to me. You can't trust cybermen.
What do you know? You're barely old enough to have read more than half a dozen books on them.
If you didn't think I was expert enough for you, why am I here?
A damn good question, Doctor Goddard. Central will be getting a good grilling from me when I get home.
If you get home.
Gentlemen, quickly!
Heavens above, Doctor. What's going on?
It's Nikki. I think her conditioning is breaking down. Blast! I need a delta wave augmenter from the TARDIS.
Doctor Goddard, can you help me carry it?
Sure.
What is...?
Back in a mo'.
What happened?
I don't know. She just collapsed.
Oh, and by the way, Administrator...
Don't do that, please. Gave me a fright. Thought you'd gone.
So sorry. Did you find anything?
What? Oh, yes. This.
I see. I wonder what it is exactly.
Well, it's... Yes, I can see that. I mean, exactly.
Back soon.
Strange man. He really is.
Controller, the new convert is ready for you.
Reporting for duty, Controller.
Mr. Carey? Oh, no. What have they done to you?
He no longer dreams or believes. Reporting for duty, Controller.
Excellent.
Well, here we are.
What about this delta wave augmenter you mentioned?
It's inside the TARDIS, Doctor Goddard.
Well, why don't you open the door and get it?
No point. She's faking.
What?
I've been around the galaxy enough times to know when I'm being baited.
She wanted access to the TARDIS. She wasn't getting it via conventional cyber threats.
I know when I'm being lied to.
So why are we here?
Because I needed to talk to you properly. Away from a cyberbomb.
And as you don't have a transponder, we should be all right here.
Talk? What about?
Oh, about you, Doctor Goddard. And why you are here.
You sure would need an expert on the Cybermen.
Oh, I congratulate you. You must have learned many lifetimes worth of knowledge in what, four years? Five at most?
I'm not as young as I look.
Something else I've been pondering about. You're invisible, aren't you?
I'm what?
Oh, not to me. Not to a human. But to the Cybermen. To Nikki Savage and the others whose sight has been augmented by alien technology.
I don't know what you're talking...
Oh, stop lying, Goddard. Who are you?
Why do you think I'm invisible?
I noticed very early on that the cybernetic Savage ignored you when you spoke. She didn't follow you when you moved.
She mentioned that there were four of us when there were five, right in front of her... eyes.
Very good.
So who are you?
Let me show you.
What are you doing?
It's okay. Just rolling up my sleeve. No tricks, no weapons. Now watch.
Impressive?
Yes.
But I confess I'm confused.
I'm giving off a mild ultraviolet frequency scrambler from all over my body, keyed to cybernetic receptors.
As you say, it's like I'm invisible around them. They can't hear me either.
It's easy enough to hide amongst Cybermen, when you are a Cyberman.
A Cyberman? How did they get the ability to do that to you?
Oh, from you. When you gave it to them.
I most certainly did not.
Ah, but that's the tragedy of all this, Doctor. You will. In about fifteen minutes time.
